chunks: And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said:
"The fasting person is in worship, even if he is sleeping on his bed, so long as he does not backbite a Muslim."

key_terms.عِبَادَةٍ: worship and devotional obedience to Allah
key_terms.نَائِمًا: sleeping or in a state of sleep
key_terms.يَغْتَبْ: to backbite or speak ill of someone in their absence

ai.seo_question: How does backbiting affect the spiritual value of fasting?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that fasting is a state of ongoing worship whose reward continues even during rest. It also emphasizes that the spiritual value of the fast is tied to ethical conduct, especially avoiding backbiting against fellow Muslims.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1772 - The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said:
"The fasting person is in a state of worship, even if he is sleeping on his bed, as long as he does not backbite a Muslim."
